sources.entry: Local Transcriber - Menu bar app that records meetings and calls and transcribes them locally with Whisper and pyannote speaker recognition, with dictation into any app.

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar app that records meetings and calls, transcribes them locally with Whisper, recognizes speakers with pyannote, and offers dictation into any app.
summary.what_it_does: Local Transcriber is a small menu bar tool for macOS that records conversations, transcribes them, and identifies who spoke, all on the Mac. It captures microphone and system audio as separate tracks, so the other participants in a call are recorded alongside the user. Transcription uses Whisper large-v3-turbo on the Apple Silicon GPU via MLX, and the README states that one hour of audio including speaker recognition takes about three to four minutes. Speaker recognition uses pyannote with a voice database that learns names so people are recognized in later recordings. It can detect video calls (Teams, Zoom, Meet and similar), offer to record, and stop when the call ends. Dictation works by holding a key, speaking, and releasing so the text appears at the cursor in any app. Optional AI evaluation (minutes, summaries) runs on a local model such as Ollama, LM Studio or MTPLX, or on a chosen cloud provider only when the user clicks, with names replaced by placeholders. Output formats include plain text, Markdown, JSON and SRT, and there is a command line interface and an MCP server for AI agents.
use_cases: dictate text into any macOS app
generate meeting minutes and action items
notable: Runs entirely on the Mac with no account, subscription, or audio upload
Records microphone and system audio as separate tracks
Speaker voice database that remembers named speakers
Dictation via hold-to-talk key into any app
Optional MCP server and command line for AI agents
caveats: Requires Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) and macOS 14 or newer; AI features need macOS 26 with Apple Intelligence
About 8 GB free disk space, 16 GB memory recommended
Local AI evaluation needs a separately installed local language model such as Ollama or LM Studio
Recording others requires their consent; the README warns secret recording is illegal in many countries
